Whether the test was seen failing first is read from the worker's transcript, not shown by a committed capture. The skeptic checks it there and runs no build to repeat it: "It should just check that the procedure of test first was followed. Not that it should be repeating the whole process, that is a fucking waste." Whether the suite runs per edit or per landed batch is an engineering choice, and per batch is in line with the rule. Every measured and repaired defect gets a gated assertion, a deferred spec-settled one an `XXX` test.
 - **The suite's verdict is the check.** A test passes or fails, as the team designed the suite, and a value that matters is asserted in the test with the mechanisms the suite already has (an `assert` in an interpreter test, `run_out_equals` in a compiled one): "what is the purpose of a test suit that you just cannot run it and get a green? If everything that's encoded in it is, is okay and it turns red if it's not, why would you have to compare some values that it outputs? Those values must be part of the test." What a test prints beyond its checks does not matter: "When the designers of the test suite decided that it passes without any additional check, it is not needed to control its outputs." So no batch compares the corpus's printed outputs, no baseline is run to compare against, and no expected-output files are added to the interpreter suite, which has none; none of it is offered to him again.
+- **Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.** "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt." Every worktree of a batch starts from one built baseline of its base, copied or seeded, never a clean build per agent (his "Duh!" to "seeding a worktree by copying a built tree rather than rebuilding it"); a skeptic never builds: it compiles only its own small programs, with the rung's build for the new code and the batch's one shared base build for the old; the second skeptic checks only the repair against its own refusal; no stage re-runs a build, a suite or a measurement on a code state another stage has already run, and no agent reads again a log of output that has not changed: "I want to eliminate all waste of this type. Where we are re-executing stuff for no reason." How a worktree is seeded and what a worker clears after an edit or a failed build is engineering, measured before it is built into the batch script (`coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`).
 - **A deeper pass, not a halt.** When something goes wrong or turns out undecided, the answer is a deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. On a red gate over a merged batch, no bisection of commits: "we should identify the source of the conflict holistically and rework that part in the merged batch", because the goal is one tree with everything running rather than the largest subset that happens to be green. On a divergence the specification does not settle, no stop: "it is not a reason to stop the climb, it is the reason to think harder, review the architecture and holistically decide on the best path forward and execute that one." What reaches him are the forks already reserved in `PLAN.md`, not new ones invented at the point of difficulty.

Rows are taken one per message with refreshers (other languages, what makes sense in a high-performance language), not in groups.
 - **A brief describes the problem, not the solution.** "How do we prevent the myopic view? … I want to have full creativity of solutions": a worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language and the library offer before a design choice reaches him; a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the library gets around it (protocol principle 2). A worker that records timings records the CPU too, so that comparisons can be guessed at.

# Climb batch 8: conformance, process and routing

## What came up in this run

### 1. The Meet Rule class: 103 to 99, though the rule cleared what it was meant to

The landed per-site lists (`explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv` at `493b4076f` and at `6416d216f`), read site by site.

**What went, 119 of the 123 overloading errors (M1 103 and L1 20).**
- Rung O's rule for functional methods, 78, exactly the record's count (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-8.md`, Q1): `FORWARD_CMP` 38, `IN` 29, `seq` 10, `SQCAP` 1, every one a top-level pair of two functional methods.

**What is left of the old 123: 4.** `isLeftZero` 2 and the full sequential ranges' `map` 2, which rung M left with rows 582 and 583 because each repair changes a walk value or needs a new type.

- The base's per-provider check kept only functional methods with a body (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:133` at `493b4076f`). An api declaration has no body, so the check read nothing in an api. In a component it skipped every declaration inherited from an api.

The repair reads every functional method in an api and the api-inherited ones in a component (`OverloadingChecker.scala:138-141` on `main`), and compares the meet without the self parameter wherever it sits (`:584-586`, `withoutSelf` at `:595-603`).
- That surfaced 102 pairs no check had read: 58 in the apis, 44 in the components (`rung-overloading-checker/REPORT.md` section 10). Rung M's juxtaposition move cleared 7 of them. 95 remain:
  - `CAP` 64, all in `RangeInternals`: `BoundedRange`'s `opr INTERSECTION(self, other: Range[\I\])` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2228`) beside `ScalarRange`'s `CAP` (`Library/RangeInternals.fsi:46`, body `RangeInternals.fss:149`) in 12 scalar range types, and beside `Range2D`'s and `Range3D`'s two each (`RangeInternals.fsi:63-64`, `:94-95`) in five types each. **The rise by cause** (the landed per-site lists, classified with the stage's own `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/classify.py`, messages compared with line numbers masked):

**Is it in the spirit? Yes.**
- The paper's instance rule, as decided, gives a parameter nothing fixes "the intersection of its upper bounds, its declared bound (`Any` if none) under the constraint of the call's static return type; never `Bottom`" (POSITIONS, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix takes its bound"). - So the 11 need two things, both on record: item 20's drop (each of the 11 calls `fail` or `builtinPrimitive`, bounded `Object`), and a checker change that passes the type the text already requires into those contexts. Only the second is new work; it is not a fork for Pavol.

### 3. The cleaning and the microGPT checks' inputs (row 576)

- `1ee3b0bc5` removed `explorations/apl/reference/dzaima/docs.txt` and `w/*.txt`. The check programs read them through a relative path, `("../../apl/reference/dzaima/docs.txt", "../../apl/reference/dzaima/w")` (`explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:19`; `explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fss:28`).

By the rule the ten files stay.
- So it is a defect of the census, not of the rule. The census followed the paths that scripts and tools name, one level deep and by their `explorations/...` spelling; it did not follow what a kept program reads, and a relative path does not match a grep for the full path. The goldens the same programs read (`explorations/run-c/goldens/`) were kept, because the check programs name them by a path the census saw.
- Nothing caught it for two days. The cleaning reached `main` at 08:12 on 2026-09-30 (`d2d5e83a8`), three minutes after batch 7b's commit stage had started its microGPT run; the gate never runs microGPT (POSITIONS, "Interpreter performance is irrelevant"); rung Q's run at 13:38 on 2026-10-02 was the first after it and stopped at FileNotFound.

- Where it belongs:

  - The lesson goes with the rule. Any later cleaning, and the planned cleaner pass of `main` (PLAN, "Housekeeping"), runs each kept tool once on the cleaned tree before it lands, and its census follows the reads of every program a kept tool runs, relative paths included.

## For Pavol

- All four rungs follow your decisions and the designers' text.
- One of your decisions did not land: `NN32` converting into `RR64`. If built, it makes `ZZ32` plus `NN32` ambiguous, against answer 8. It is item 37 on your list, default "not built". A probe before the batch would have caught it.
- The Meet Rule count moved only from 103 to 99, but the rule worked:
  - it cleared the 78 errors expected, and the other fixes cleared 41 more;
  - the corrected checker now sees 95 real library gaps it never read before, above all the range types' `CAP` (64) and `IN` (30). That is library work for the next batch.
- The 29 new errors in the library's code come from the paper's rule meeting the `Object` bounds that batch 7 wrote to get `Bottom`. Nothing that ran before is lost:
  - dropping those bounds (item 20) clears 18;
  - the other 11 also need `()` passed into an `if` without `else`. The specification already requires that, so item 36 is mostly settled.
- The cleaning deleted the microGPT checks' input files because it took them for captures. They should be restored.
- The baseline for batch 9:
  - 35 builds, about 85 minutes of machine time; 22 of them rebuilt code another agent had already built;
  - the gate ran twice, and the second skeptics redid their whole list;
  - about 0.5M and an hour of waiting in total.
- The review's one blocking finding cost 0.53M and 36 minutes. It fixed one sentence the gather already knew was wrong.
- Cost: 7.7M written, 21 agents, 7 h 37 min, against the record's estimate of 6M to 8M. One cache miss accounts for 0.46M of it.

The review is in commit `49cd5595a`, at `/home/user/fortress/explorations/reviews/batch-8-review.md`. Main had moved to `3de0a9cbf` before I committed, but `git log origin/main..main` showed only my commit, so no rebase was needed. It is pushed to `main` and `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8`.

Notes for the coordinator:
- The commit stage's microGPT run finished at 20:40: both checks passed 40 of 40, and the inputs were removed again.
- Ten new rows have no line in `PLAN.md`: 563, 564, 565, 567, 571, 573, 574, 578, 579 and 586. Phase 5's code-generation line also does not name row 559 or 566. Part 3 of the review proposes a home for each.
- `PLAN.md:85` still says rung B's bounds "become unnecessary and may stay".
